inspections.anchor: Consider the graph H that is obtained by removing the edges of a Hamiltonian cycle from K5,5
inspections.note: K_{5,5} minus a Hamiltonian cycle: the smallest graph for which Sidorenko's conjecture is open.

problem.text: Lovasz's question which graphs H make h_H(.)^{1/m} a norm, and its application to Sidorenko's conjecture.

claims.text: Theorem 2.8: norming is equivalent to a Holder inequality; Theorem 2.9: complete bipartite graphs and hypercubes are weakly norming, closure under bi-products; Theorem 2.10: a weakly norming graph has equal degrees on each part and a subgraph density condition; weakly norming graphs satisfy Sidorenko and stronger subgraph inequalities (Theorem 2.14).

assumptions.text: Bipartite graphs with a fixed bipartition; functions on products of probability spaces; the tensor power trick.

methods.text: Holder-type inequalities and tensor powers; induction on the hypercube dimension through Cauchy-Schwarz reductions.

limitations.text: Norming requires biregularity, so it cannot reach graphs with unequal degrees in a part; the paper leaves open whether every edge-transitive bipartite graph is weakly norming and whether K_{5,5} minus a Hamiltonian cycle is weakly norming.

relevance.text: The biregularity condition of Theorem 2.10 is the boundary of the norming method, and K_{5,5} minus a Hamiltonian cycle is recorded as the smallest open case of Sidorenko's conjecture; both enter the candidate comparison of this exploration.
